output.title: Retrieval quality is a workflow constraint, not a nice-to-have
output.body:
If an AI tool has to look things up to do useful work, retrieval quality is part of the workflow design, not an afterthought. In plain terms: when it searches documents, emails, FAQs, or prior records, it has to pull back the right material consistently, or the answer looks neat and lands wrong. That means rework for you, or a confident mistake.

For a small business owner, the practical question is not “can AI answer this?” It is “can it find the right source every time this task runs?” If one recurring job makes you search more than one place for the answer, retrieval is already a design constraint. That is true for customer questions, invoice checks, and lead follow-up.

The next step is simple: pick one recurring workflow and audit the source material behind it. Are the documents named clearly, grouped sensibly, and kept current? If the inputs are messy, automation usually moves the manual work earlier instead of removing it. Bareni’s self-built local knowledge-assistant demo shows grounded answers with sources on synthetic data, but the public route is locked, so treat that as a demo pattern, not a deployed service. The useful test is still the same: can you trust where the answer came from?
